fact: DLA Piper states that Cape Verde's Data Protection Law (Law 133/V/2001 as amended, including by Law 41/VIII/2013 and Law 121/IX/2021) permits international transfer of personal data only to a country with an adequate level of protection, or otherwise with the data subject's consent or in listed situations such as contract necessity or vital interests; the document gives no date for the rule, so its published date of 2025-01-16 is used.

Lei n.º 41/VIII/2013, published 17 September 2013 and in force thirty days later, amends the general data protection law (Lei 133/V/2001) so that article 19 allows transfer abroad only to a country assuring an adequate level of protection, the CNPD deciding which foreign states do, and article 20 lets the CNPD permit transfer elsewhere on consent, contract necessity, public interest, vital interests or a public register, or authorise it where the controller gives sufficient guarantees such as adequate contractual clauses.
system: Lei n.º 133/V/2001 as amended by Lei n.º 41/VIII/2013
